info.title: BlastRadius API
info.description: BlastRadius Phase 1: safe, read-only ingestion of public GitHub repositories with real Python dependency extraction (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, uv.lock).

post.summary: Ingest a public GitHub repository and extract its Python dependencies
post.description:
Run the ingestion pipeline for one repository revision.

The endpoint is synchronous on purpose: retrieval and parsing are bounded by
configured timeouts, and FastAPI runs it in a worker thread so the event
loop is never blocked. Failures raise typed errors which the application
error handlers translate into the documented error envelope.

get.description:
Return whether the configured FalkorDB graph is reachable.

This probe never raises: when the graph is unavailable it reports
``connected: false`` so that callers can degrade gracefully.

post.summary: Persist a Phase 1 ingestion result into the graph
post.description:
Persist a Phase 1 :class:`~app.models.ingestion.IngestionResult` into FalkorDB.

The request body must contain the serialised ingestion result under the
``result`` key: either the domain ``IngestionResult`` shape or the public
``RepositoryIngestResponse`` shape returned by
``POST /api/v1/repositories/ingest``, which converts losslessly.  The
write is idempotent: re-ingesting the same repository at the same commit
upserts instead of duplicating nodes or relationships.

post.summary: Ask a security question about one analysis
post.description: Runs the Phase 4B evidence-grounded agent: the question and the MCP-discovered read-only tool schemas are sent to the configured LLM provider, tool calls are validated (allowlist + analysis scope) and executed through MCP, and the final answer must pass a deterministic grounding check against the collected evidence. The agent never writes to the graph and never invents vulnerability data.

get.summary: Look up vulnerabilities for one package (live OSV, no graph writes)
get.description:
Query the OSV.dev database for one package, by ecosystem/name/version.

Without ``version`` the results are name-level matches and are reported as
``match_type="name"``/``confirmed=false``; they are informational and not
written anywhere.

post.summary: Ingest OSV vulnerabilities for one analysis's resolved packages
post.description:
Run a targeted OSV sync for one persisted analysis.

Every resolved package of the analysis is queried on OSV (batched
discovery, then full-record hydration).  Only version-confirmed matches —
OSV confirmed the exact resolved version is affected — become
``AFFECTED_BY`` edges.  Packages without a resolved version are reported
and untouched.  The run is idempotent: repeating it refreshes stored
records instead of duplicating them.

get.summary: Trace impact chains from affected packages to downstream dependents
get.description:
Explainable paths: vulnerable package -> dependents impacted through it.

``hop_count == 0`` rows are the directly affected packages; ``hop_count >= 1``
rows depend on them through actual graph relationships.  Every path names
the vulnerability id supporting the conclusion.

get.summary: Return one stored vulnerability record and its affected components
get.description:
One vulnerability exactly as mirrored from OSV, plus its graph components.

The components are returned across *all* repositories and analyses where the
vulnerability was seen: the query is intentionally unscoped so a consumer can
see every affected component for a shared OSV record.  Each component row
carries its own ``repository_id`` and ``commit_sha``; callers needing an
analysis-scoped view should filter on those, or use
``GET /analyses/{analysis_id}/vulnerabilities`` instead.

post.description: Builds the deterministic title/body for one server-issued fix group or finding id, validates the canonical repository target and its GitHub accessibility (read-only), and persists a digest-bound PREVIEWED action. No GitHub write is performed. Caller-supplied security facts are rejected.

post.summary: Confirm and execute one previewed GitHub issue
post.description: Revalidates the analysis evidence, requires the dedicated confirmation secret and the exact payload digest, atomically reserves the action and creates the issue through the GitHub REST API. Expired, altered, replayed or concurrently executed actions are rejected; a repeated confirmation of a completed action returns the stored issue result.
